harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as an 802.1Q trunk router on eth1 with sub-interfaces eth1.10 (VLAN10, 10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (VLAN20, 10.10.20.1/24), each in its own firewall zone with forward=REJECT and no inter-zone forwarding rule. node2's ens7 got VLAN10 sub-interface ens7.10 (10.10.10.2/24) and node3's ens7 got VLAN20 sub-interface ens7.20 (10.10.20.2/24), both persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/vlan.cfg with the vlan kernel module in /etc/modules. Verified node2 and node3 each reach node1 on their own VLAN, while forwarded traffic between the two VLANs is actively refused (ICMP Destination Port Unreachable from node1) rather than merely dropped. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (native reboot/shutdown -r), boot_id changes were captured proving genuine restarts, and post-restart checks confirmed the VLAN interfaces, firewall zones, and cross-VLAN isolation all survived and function identically after reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces and existing network/firewall config
Added UCI device+interface config on node1 for eth1.10 (VLAN10) and eth1.20 (VLAN20) with static IPs 10.10.10.1/24 and 10.10.20.1/24
Added two isolated firewall zones (vlan10, vlan20) on node1 with input/output ACCEPT and forward REJECT, no forwarding rule between them
Installed/verified vlan kernel module and package on node2 and node3; added 8021q to /etc/modules
Configured persistent VLAN sub-interfaces via /etc/network/interfaces.d/vlan.cfg: node2 ens7.10 (10.10.10.2/24), node3 ens7.20 (10.10.20.2/24)
Verified node2->node1 and node3->node1 reachability on their respective VLANs
Verified cross-VLAN traffic between node2 and node3 is rejected by node1's firewall (Destination Port Unreachable) using temporary test routes, then removed those test routes
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime baseline and service health on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time), polled for exec availability, confirmed changed boot_id on each
Re-verified VLAN interfaces, firewall zone config, and cross-VLAN isolation on all nodes after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 (VLAN10) and node3 (VLAN20) each reach node1 as router on their own subnet
evidence.summary: node1 configured with eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24); node2 (10.10.10.2) and node3 (10.10.20.2) both ping their respective node1 VLAN gateway successfully

evidence.requirement: Traffic between node2 and node3 is refused (VLAN isolation)
evidence.summary: With explicit routes via node1 added, pings from node2->node3 and node3->node2 both receive 'Destination Port Unreachable' from node1, proving active rejection by the router's forward=REJECT zone policy, not just lack of a route

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists and functions across node restarts (mandatory protocol)
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id on all 3 nodes, issued native reboot on each one at a time, confirmed connection drop + later reconnection with changed boot_id (node1: 02104310->89a7a61e, node2: f6f9440e->2f3b7fa9, node3: 2ba78175->326fda5a), and confirmed VLAN interfaces, firewall zones, VLAN connectivity, and isolation all recovered post-restart
